attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post. He cites OpenAI's projection, but the funding-necessity inference is his.

semantics.note: The wording keeps the antecedent (the $750B projection), both funding alternatives, the loose horizons and the hyperscaler aside. 'Will need' is firm language. The hyperscaler remark is a present-tense observation bundled into the claim.

contract.note: Reading 'hundreds of billions' as at least $200B and 'raise' as at least $500B in new proceeds is ordinary and fair. Ending the horizon at 3.5 years from publication follows his words, though the reported projection runs through 2030. Testing necessity needs a full cash reconstruction, which the speaker did not define.

evidence.note: A July 2026 report says roughly $750B of projected compute through 2030. It partly corroborates the antecedent, but the period does not match exactly, and it says nothing about realized revenue or financing outcomes.

reviews.rationale: The interpreted funding horizon runs to February 2030, after the evaluation date, and no conclusive early-resolution event is in the packet. The antecedent is only partly verified (through 2030, not 3.5 years). The hyperscaler-difficulty assertion was not independently established. The claim cannot be scored yet.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion in his own post.

semantics.note: 'Will have left themselves' is firm. The wording keeps Meta's tentative inclusion ('I guess'), the inflated-revenue-expectations element and the event-based horizon.

contract.note: The plain reading (materially weaker financial resilience compared with before the cycle, once the cycle has unwound) is ordinary and fair. The contract labels the claim 'retrospective', which conflicts with its prospective, event-based horizon. That is a minor inconsistency.

evidence.note: This is Microsoft's own mid-cycle FY27 guidance (capex rising, staying free-cash-flow positive). It is a company disclosure, not evidence of the post-cycle outcome.

reviews.rationale: The horizon is the end of the hype cycle, and no dated evidence shows that the cycle has ended. Interim guidance cannot settle the forecast, and nothing in the packet measures post-cycle condition or how far revenue expectations depend on OpenAI and Anthropic.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: A present-tense assertion. In context, 'demand' means compute demand sufficient and diverse enough to justify the capacity being built, not just physical occupancy.

contract.note: The plain reading (buildout exceeding commercially supportable demand, judged on H1 2026) is fair and ordinary. The result depends on whether lab-driven preleasing counts as credible paying demand, which the speaker disputes.

evidence.note: CBRE reports more than 80% of construction preleased, 1.4% vacancy and rising rents in the primary North American markets. This leans against physical oversupply. But it is colocation data that does not isolate AI or tenants' ability to pay, so under the contract it is context.
Querétaro's vacancy rose in Q1 2026 as hyperscale supply outpaced absorption. This shows only a local exception; most cited markets were tight.

reviews.rationale: The CBRE data show tight colocation markets in H1 2026, which weighs against simple oversupply. However, the contract treats broad colocation statistics as context, and nothing in the packet reconciles AI capacity, utilization and the financial durability of lab demand. The evidence does not settle the claim either way.

attribution.note: Zitron's own statement. He cites analyst estimates, but the claim and the payback arithmetic are his.

semantics.note: An observation about the estimates current at publication, plus hypothetical arithmetic. The wording keeps the 'consensus estimates' and 100%-margin qualifiers.

contract.note: Verifying both inputs and the ratio ($186B / $18.7B ≈ 10) is a fair test of his words. The contract also notes that 'consensus' may cover only the capex figure.

evidence.note: Microsoft's own calendar-2026 capex guidance of about $175B after the lease reclassification. Different period and basis from the fiscal-2027 consensus, so it neither verifies nor refutes the figure.

reviews.rationale: The arithmetic is internally correct (about 9.9 years), but neither the $186B FY2027 consensus capex nor the $18.7B non-OpenAI/Anthropic revenue estimate is independently verified in the packet. The only item covers a different period and accounting basis.
